page: Amazon Web Services m8ine.large is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The server is driven by an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Its compute profile consists of 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local instance storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be addressed through attached network-based block volumes. Network performance features a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps, providing consistent connectivity without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included.

With its standard balanced memory ratio and dedicated Intel compute resources, the m8ine.large is architecturally configured for steady baseline workloads. These specifications make it suitable for standard web serving tiers, microservices, lightweight application backends, and balanced general-purpose business applications that do not require high local disk IOPS or GPU compute.
